## Chosen behavior

1. **Reject tow and salvage of a currently occupied target before mutation.** Give a clear instruction to exit safely and approach the exterior collar, or use the existing paid patch where eligible. Do not force exit/teleport, bypass suit-depth/clearance limits, erase ownership or carry the occupant through a new untested tow feature. Preserve currently valid occupied **repair** and reserve-cell behavior; do not impose a new exit requirement on those safe actions.
2. **Protect accepted old active operations.** If a loaded/current operation targets an occupied hull, stop/cancel the operation before any hull movement, with one truthful notice/guidance; retain original hull/player pose, cargo/modules/charge/air/maintenance/knowledge/losses. No tick may become invalid or grant free service. Do not weaken the codec or silently fix already-invalid imports. Cover approach/ready/tow where relevant; never repeatedly emit a cancellation notice after the operation is gone.
3. **Make Hold truthful.** Disable or otherwise clearly mark occupied tow/salvage as unavailable, explaining safe exit/local-collar access. Keep field patch and useful reserve/service information available under their existing rules. Simulation enforcement remains authoritative even if UI is bypassed. Preserve semantic focus behavior and all unrelated UI/actions. Do not claim the safe exit is always possible at the current depth/obstruction.
4. **Keep unoccupied recovery working.** After a legitimate safe exit, local tow/attach and empty-frame salvage retain their existing costs, full swept route, final mooring, losses/investments and exactly-once semantics. A refused action changes only normal feedback/events; it must not consume stock, alter an existing operation or discard cargo. The separate legacy-operation cancellation happens during update and is explicitly recorded.
